title: Identifiability Limits of Physics-Informed Inference for Spatial Stochastic Dynamics from Static Snapshots
abstract: arXiv:2607.01749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Despite increasing scale and resolution, many biological measurements provide only a static snapshot of molecular positions rather than the dynamics that produced them. By combining flexible representations with mechanistic constraints, physics-informed machine learning offers a promising route to inferring these dynamics from static snapshots. Motivated by subcellular imaging of gene expression, we ask when a static spatial pattern of molecules can identify spatially varying diffusivity, creation, destruction, and boundary exchange, and how different inference schemes perform on the task. A structural identifiability analysis shows that distributed sources are non-identifiable, whereas a point source such as a transcription site can restore identifiability. These limits are further shaped by seemingly innocuous modeling choices: the boundary conditions, the spatial regularity of the underlying dynamics, and even the stochastic

translated_title: 基于静态快照的空间随机动力学物理信息推断的可辨识性极限
translated_abstract: 尽管测量规模和分辨率不断提升，许多生物学测量仅能提供分子位置的静态快照，而非产生这些快照的动力学过程。通过将灵活的表示方法与机制约束相结合，物理信息机器学习为从静态快照推断这些动力学过程提供了一条有前景的途径。受基因表达亚细胞成像的启发，我们探讨了分子的静态空间模式何时能够辨识空间变化的扩散率、生成、销毁以及边界交换过程，并研究了不同的推断方案在该任务上的表现。结构性可辨识性分析表明，分布式源是不可辨识的，而诸如转录位点这样的点源则可以恢复可辨识性。这些极限还进一步受到看似无关紧要的建模选择的影响：边界条件、底层动力学的空间正则性，甚至随机性……
tldr: 本研究通过结构性可辨识性分析揭示了利用物理信息机器学习从分子静态空间快照推断空间随机动力学的根本极限：分布式源本质上不可辨识，而点源（如转录位点）可恢复可辨识性，且这些极限还受边界条件、空间正则性等建模选择的制约。
en_tdlr: This study establishes structural identifiability limits for physics-informed inference of spatial stochastic dynamics from static molecular snapshots: distributed sources are fundamentally non-identifiable, point sources such as transcription sites can restore identifiability, and seemingly innocuous modeling choices like boundary conditions further shape these limits.
